Title: Great sound, weak mechanical design, bad warranty
Review Text:
The XM5 sound amazing and good microphone quality.  I have had these headphones since launch, so for 8 months.  I have loved them for 8 months.  I take them off with two hands, and always store them in its case.  To my horror two days ago, I found that the ear cup connection to the headband has come apart.  The plastic that surround the molded in or vibration welded fastener had split.  Now my earcups do not stay in place.
I brought this to the attention of Sony warranty and they tell me because it is a physical defect and they can not confirm that it is from physical abuse, they will not warranty it.  At my expense, I have to send it to their authorized service depot, and pay for it to get it repaired myself.
I was already wary about the plastic materials used for fear of its potential weakness in material.  After 8 months, this confirmed my suspicion.  If Best Buy could let me post pictures of the failure I would.  It is appalling that this is how Sony supports one of its flagship products.  I do not think I will buy a Sony product again.  If you buy it, purchase an extended replacement warranty with it.
So buyer beware.  I am no longer a fan of Sony products

Title: Expensive but Seriously Lacking
Review Text: Most expensive headphones I have ever bought.  And will never ever buy sony headphones again.  Two weeks of trouble shooting.  These cannot be returned to best buy and the best Sony can do is replace them but the issues seem built into these headphones.  The design and feel is great.  The listening sound quality as well.  But if you purchase these expensive headphones to do any serious work - like calling on phones or using in videochats then avoid them at all costs.  They are NOT designed for this and sony and other reviewers should be honest about that.  In two weeks of ownership every voice call the user on the other end complains of echo of their own voice.  Have disabled all of the high end features of these expensive headsets and nothing helps.  In video chats the headset works at first but then disconnects part way through and you can't get reconnected without completely rebooting the chat.  You can connect these to the computer with a wired connection (included) and it works fine for listening but there is no in-line mic (not well advertised but these sony headphones don't allow wired connection with mic, which is shocking for the price).  So my options are use my old bose headphones (which have always worked fine as bluetooth) or use these with a wire connection and a separate mic.  None of this is what one should expect from VERY expensive headphones that are advertsized for voice and video calls as well as listening.  Avoid these unless you have money to burn.  Sony seems uninterested in the issue (and there are multiple threads online about this but one only finds those after one purchases and runs into problems).

Title: My new favorite headphones
Review Text:
[This review was collected as part of a promotion.] I’ve had these headphones for a while now and I honestly understand why they get so much hype. The sound is really clear and immersive, and the noise cancellation is probably my favorite feature. It makes such a difference on flights, at the gym, or even when I just want to focus at home.

I also love how easy they are to use. The touch controls are convenient, the battery lasts a long time, and switching between using them at home, at the gym, and while traveling has been super easy.

They are very comfortable overall, although after wearing them for a long time I sometimes notice a little pressure on the top of my head from the headband. It’s not a dealbreaker for me, especially considering how good the headphones are in every other way.

I also own the Sony WF-1000XM5 earbuds, which I really like as well, but the experience is completely different. The earbuds are great when I want something compact and convenient, while the WH-1000XM5 feel more immersive and are especially nice for longer listening sessions and travel. I’m glad I have both because they each have their own strengths.

Overall, I’m really happy with this purchase. They’ve become one of those things I use almost every day and would definitely recommend them.

Title: Excellent sound
Review Text:
Excellent sound, very poor durability

Unfortunately, the build quality has been a huge disappointment. The hinge/plastic near the ear cup has broken multiple times during normal use. I have had to repair it with glue several times just to keep using them. Now the microphone/audio during calls is also starting to fail.
For headphones in this price range, I expected them to last much longer. Great sound alone is not enough if the product keeps breaking.
I would not recommend them unless Sony improves the durability of the hinge design.

Title: Avoid this product
Review Text:
I bought these in July 2025, expecting "industry-leading" quality for a premium price. Less than a year later, the slider arm has already snapped during normal use.
​What’s most frustrating is that I have a pair of "budget" brand headphones that have lasted years and feel significantly sturdier than these. After doing some research, it’s clear this is a common design flaw with the WH-1000XM5. The plastic swivel point is far too fragile for daily wear and tear.
​The noise canceling and sound are great, but it doesn't matter how good they sound if they are held together by tape within a few months. If you are looking for durability, look elsewhere—or at least look at the previous XM4 model which has a much more reliable hinge. Very disappointed in Sony's build quality on this flagship model.

Title: Don't
Review Text:
Great sound.
Perhaps the worst purchase of my entire life.

When your fragile hinges break in less than a year of gentle use and Sony will blame you for the damage and refuse to honour their own guarantee.

It's so widespread and well documented that this particular model is subject to a class action lawsuit in New York (google 'Kanter v. Sony Corporation Of America et al').

Sony will not honour your consumer rights.
If you are in a similar situation I also encourage you to file a complaint: https://www.gov.uk/consumer-protection-rights
I could never in good conscience recommend anyone purchase anything from this company.
